newsitem.title: CHINA: China flood damage hits record $26.5 billion.
newsitem.headline: China flood damage hits record $26.5 billion.

text.p: Summer floods that ravaged much of southern and northeastern China earlier this year caused a record 220 billion yuan ($26.5 billion) in damage, the China Daily said on Saturday.

The losses were nearly triple those of devastating floods in 1991 that caused 80 billion yuan ($9.6 billion) in damage, the newspaper quoted Sun Zhongzu, spokesman for the Ministry of Water Resources, as saying.
Raging floods from June to August had laid waste huge swathes of land in about half of China's provinces and regions, Sun said.
"The more quickly China's economy develops, the more costly the destruction will become if better anti-flood measures are not taken," Sun warned.
China should step up efforts to build water control projects on major rivers and lakes to try to reduce the impact of the seasonal deluges, he said.
The three months of flooding killed at least 2,700 people, injured more than 32,200 and left hundreds of thousands homeless, according to the latest official figures.
The surging waters also wiped out tens of thousands of tonnes of grain and inundated vast tracts of precious cropland, but China still predicts a bumper harvest this year.
China's largest insurer, the People's Insurance Company of China Group, has paid more than 3.3 billion yuan ($398 million) by early October to cover losses caused by the floods.
